metadata.title: FleetTrack System Security Plan [DEGRADED VARIANT: partial_v2]
metadata.remarks:
STRONG-GRADE fixture SSP for the PCEF dissertation project's Stage B discriminant test. FleetTrack is a demo B2B fleet/driver location-tracking SaaS skeleton; it is not a real product. Implementation statements below cite real file paths and function names from the FleetTrack repo where the behavior was actually built and verified (see PROGRESS.md); components explicitly marked 'narrative-only' were deliberately NOT built and describe an assumed organizational process for the PoC scenario only, per FleetTrack/CLAUDE.md. Partial/broken grades are produced by editing this document directly, not by rebuilding the system.
Generated by validation/degrade_ssp.py from the strong FleetTrack SSP. v2: statements with index%3==1 deleted; kept text cut to its first half of sentences, artefacts generalised.

system-characteristics.description: A B2B SaaS backend that lets a client company track its own drivers and vehicles for logistics purposes. Backend-only (FastAPI + SQLite) plus one thin, read-only, server-rendered dashboard. Multi-tenant: each client company (tenant) sees only its own drivers, vehicles, and trip data.

authorization-boundary.description: The FastAPI backend (app/), its SQLite database, and the Jinja2 dashboard. Driver mobile devices are out of the boundary (unmanaged, BYOD-equivalent) - scripts/simulate_telemetry.py stands in for them. The mapping-vendor and cloud-host components are narrative-only and outside any real boundary.

system-implementation.remarks: This is a partial implementation: a minimal skeleton built specifically to ground a strong-grade SSP with real, citable artefacts. See FleetTrack/PROGRESS.md for the full build log and verification notes for every claim made below.

control-implementation.description: Control implementation for FleetTrack, strong grade. Citations are real (file path / function name) wherever the underlying behavior was actually built and verified per PROGRESS.md; entries and by-components marked NARRATIVE-ONLY or KNOWN GAP were deliberately not built and are flagged as such rather than fabricated.

by-components.description: Four account types are defined and enforced: a named function, driver, a named function, a named function (a configuration file, Role enum; a configuration file, a named function).

Account use is monitored via the audit log: every create/update/delete on drivers and vehicles, and every read of trips/reports/telemetry-derived dashboard data, is attributed to the acting user (a configuration file, a named function; see AU-2 below).

A single reusable dependency chain enforces access: a named function (a standard mechanism/cookie verification), a named function(*allowed) (role gate, 403 on mismatch), and a named function (cross-tenant guard, 403 unless caller's a named function matches the target resource's or caller is a named function) - all in a configuration file.
The dashboard reuses the same a named function/a named function dependencies as the JSON API rather than separate access-control logic (a configuration file).
a standard mechanism-based authentication: a named function/a named function (a configuration file, HS256 via PyJWT).
Audit records are queryable directly from the a named function table (no dedicated review UI was built for the skeleton).

statements.remarks: Manual/ad hoc review only in the current skeleton - records exist and are complete (see AU-2), but no scheduled review process, alerting, or reporting tool was built. Partial coverage: logging is real, review tooling is not.

Driver and vehicle identity records (name, contact, employee ID, vehicle registration, assignment) are correctable via an endpoint and an endpoint (a configuration file, a configuration file), each RBAC-scoped to the Fleet Manager role and the record's own company. No automated data-quality check (e.g.

DriverCreate.a named function (a configuration file) is a required, non-Optional field with no default; Driver.a named function (a configuration file, non-nullable column) enforces it at the DB layer too. an endpoint without it returns 422 before any row is created - verified directly.

Telemetry is collected only via authenticated driver POSTs to /telemetry, scoped to the driver's own assigned vehicle within their own company (a configuration file, a named function) - no broader collection than the stated logistics purpose.
